skill.name: prd
skill.description: Create structured Product Requirements Documents for software and AI features using discovery questions, measurable requirements, technical specifications, user stories, risks, and roadmaps.
skill.summary: Turn product ideas into measurable requirements, technical plans, user stories, and phased roadmaps.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code formatting, or ordinary prose. SKILL.md contains no executable scripts, command invocation, prompt injection, or intent-level security concern.

static_findings.snippet: - **User Stories**: `As a [user], I want to [action] so that [benefit].`
- **Hallucinate Constraints**: If the user didn't specify a tech stack, ask or label it as `TBD`.
Use concrete, measurable criteria. Avoid "fast", "easy", or "intuitive".

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 56 opens a Markdown diff fence that illustrates vague and concrete requirements. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any command.
Line 65 closes the Markdown diff fence opened on line 56. The fenced content is documentation and contains no executable command.
Line 82 uses inline Markdown code to display a user-story sentence template. It contains no command syntax or execution instruction.
Line 114 formats the placeholder TBD as inline code. It neither executes a command nor directs the agent to execute one.
Line 138 lists tool names as inline Markdown within an example PRD. It does not request tool execution or provide shell syntax.
Line 54 is writing guidance that asks for measurable requirements. It performs no system, environment, host, or resource reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Vague product ideas cause unclear scope, weak acceptance criteria, and delivery risk. This skill turns stakeholder input into a structured, measurable Product Requirements Document.
actual_capabilities: Asks discovery questions about the core problem, success metrics, constraints, and timing.
Transforms product input into an executive summary with a problem statement, proposed solution, and measurable success criteria.
Defines user personas, user stories, acceptance criteria, and explicit non-goals.
Documents architecture, integrations, security, privacy, tools, and evaluation requirements.
Identifies technical risks, dependencies, hidden complexity, and phased rollout milestones.
Supports software systems and AI-powered features through a consistent PRD structure.
limitations: The workflow requires at least two clarifying questions before drafting a PRD.
It does not independently validate feasibility, legal compliance, budgets, or market assumptions.
It creates requirements and plans but does not implement the product or generate project code.
The fixed PRD structure may require adaptation for an organization's internal approval process.

use_cases.title: Scope a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Convert stakeholder goals into measurable requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and rollout phases.

use_cases.title: Align Technical Delivery
use_cases.description: Document architecture, integrations, security expectations, dependencies, technical risks, and test requirements before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan an AI Capability
use_cases.description: Define model or tool requirements, evaluation metrics, quality thresholds, privacy controls, and failure handling for an AI feature.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Feature PRD
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for [feature]. First ask at least two questions about the problem, target users, success metrics, and constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new software feature

prompt_templates.title: Turn an Idea into Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [product idea] into a scoped PRD. Include measurable outcomes, user stories, acceptance criteria, dependencies, non-goals, and an MVP rollout.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning from an early product concept

prompt_templates.title: Specify an AI Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PRD for [AI feature]. Define tools, data handling, evaluation datasets, quality thresholds, latency targets, costs, safeguards, and failure modes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed requirements for an AI-powered capability

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Production Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production PRD for [system]. Analyze architecture, integrations, privacy, security, operational risks, testing, observability, dependencies, and phased release criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a complex production system

output_examples.input: Create a PRD for saved searches in a business analytics dashboard.
output: Problem: Analysts repeatedly rebuild common filters, increasing reporting time and creating inconsistent results.
Success criteria: Reduce repeated filter setup time by 60 percent and achieve 40 percent weekly adoption among active analysts.
User story: As an analyst, I want to save named filters so I can reopen recurring reports quickly.
Non-goal: The first release will not support sharing saved searches across organizations.

output_examples.input: Plan an AI assistant that summarizes customer support conversations.
output: Solution: Generate concise summaries with customer intent, actions taken, unresolved issues, and cited conversation turns.
Evaluation: At least 90 percent of summaries must preserve critical facts in a reviewed benchmark of 500 conversations.
Privacy: Redact configured personal data before model processing and retain summaries according to existing support policies.
Rollout: Begin with agent review, measure correction rates, and enable automatic saving only after quality targets remain stable.

best_practices: Provide the business problem, target users, constraints, and expected outcome before drafting.
Replace subjective words with measurable thresholds for performance, quality, adoption, and reliability.
Review the first draft with product, engineering, design, security, and operations stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not request a final PRD while withholding essential context or refusing discovery questions.
Do not present unverified assumptions about technology, budgets, compliance, or deadlines as confirmed requirements.
Do not omit non-goals, acceptance criteria, dependencies, or measurable success metrics.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the problem, target users, desired outcome, constraints, known dependencies, deadline, and available success metrics.

faq.question: Can this skill create PRDs for AI features?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers tools, APIs, evaluation strategy, quality targets, data handling, privacy, latency, costs, and failure risks.

faq.question: Will it ask clarifying questions?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires at least two questions before drafting when essential context is missing.

faq.question: Does it generate implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It produces product and technical requirements that guide implementation.

faq.question: Can I use an existing draft?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the draft and ask for missing sections, measurable criteria, clearer scope, stronger risks, or a complete revision.

faq.question: Does the PRD include security and privacy?
faq.answer: Yes. The technical specification includes security, privacy, data handling, integrations, authentication, and relevant compliance requirements.
